tells: Scope tube, rings and bolt body read as polished chrome/silver with sharp mirror-like environment streaks; real scopes are matte black hard-anodized, bolts are dull blued/nitrided steel
Eyepiece is an empty dark disc with no lens coating reflections, no internal glass depth, no reticle hint
Chassis is flat untextured OD/grey with uniform paint and no edge wear, dust, fingerprints, or cerakote micro-sheen variation
Hard faceted silhouettes and low-segment curves on ocular bell and rings; many edges are razor-sharp with no bevel catch-light
Scale of small parts off: bolt knob is a perfect knurled sphere, screws are oversized plain cylinders, picatinny rail slots are shallow and soft
Lighting is flat grey studio void with no contact shadow, no surface, no depth of field; the wide FOV at 35 cm shows no lens falloff or defocus that a real camera at that distance would have
Eyepiece is a flat black void: no reticle, no exit pupil, no multi-coated lens reflections (green/magenta/amber glints), no visible glass surface
Eyecup rim polygonal (visible facets on silhouette) with a thin white specular outline that looks like CG rim light
Rubber eyecup has no texture, molding seams or printing; uniform black
No defocus at the near distance; everything is equally sharp, which a real close-up lens could not do
Floating object on a seamless grey void with no shadow or ground contact
Chassis colour is a flat desaturated grey-green with no material response; reads as clay/primer render
Butt stock block is boxy with unbeveled hard corners; cheek riser looks like a plain cube
At this distance overall proportions are plausible (bipod, suppressor/brake, scope), which is why confidence is not higher
Chassis surfaces are perfectly flat panels with a fine uniform noise grain that reads as procedural texture, not cerakote/anodize; no wear on edges, screw heads or high spots
Edges of chassis panels are either knife-sharp or have a single uniform small bevel; real machined aluminium shows consistent chamfers with bright edge catch-lights
Pistol grip has an unrealistic faceted/stippled pattern and blocky finger grooves; looks like low-poly placeholder
Objective lens is a uniform deep blue disc without layered coating reflections or the inner tube and lens element depth
Scope body is semi-gloss plastic-black with a CG-smooth highlight; turret knurling is too regular and coarse
Magazine is a featureless box with simple grooves; no follower, cartridge visible, witness holes or markings
No markings, serials, logos or engraving anywhere; real rifles always show at least serial/caliber stamping
Bolt body and ocular housing again read as mirror chrome against matte chassis; inconsistent with a tactical rifle
Bipod legs are glossy black cylinders with overly clean segments; feet are simple pucks without rubber tread or wear
Rifle floats with bipod deployed in mid-air, no ground, no contact shadow; bipod deployed but not resting on anything is a strong CG tell
Stock and buttpad: flat, boxy, untextured rubber pad with no ribbing detail; spacer plates look like solid black blocks
Uniform even lighting without any bounce colour, dust, or imperfection; colour of chassis is primer-like light grey-green

priorities: Fix metal materials: scope tube, rings, ocular housing and bolt body read as polished chrome. Make the scope matte/satin black hard-anodized aluminium (roughness ~0.45-0.6, broad soft highlights) and the bolt dull nitrided/blued steel (dark grey, roughness ~0.35-0.5) with a slightly brighter polished bolt-raceway wear band only

Build real optics: lenses need glass with layered anti-reflective coatings (faint green/magenta/amber reflections), visible internal lens elements and tube depth, and a reticle/exit pupil visible in the eyepiece view; the ADS view must not be a black void

Chassis finish: replace the flat procedural grain with a believable cerakote/anodize response (subtle sheen variation, micro-roughness breakup), and add edge wear on corners, screw heads, mag well lip, bolt handle path, plus light dust/fingerprints/handling smudges

Consistent machined chamfers on all chassis, stock and rail edges (1-2 mm with crisp catch-lights); remove knife-sharp edges and visible polygon facets on round parts (eyecup, bells, rings, bipod feet) by raising segment counts
Add markings: serial/caliber stamping on the action, turret numerals and hash marks, scope magnification ring numbers, rail slot numbers, small generic maker-style logo; empty surfaces scream CG
Rework the pistol grip and buttpad: proper rubber overmold texture/stippling, realistic finger contour, ribbed rubber recoil pad; stock spacers and cheek riser need hardware and real thickness detail
Small-part scale and detail: thinner screw heads with hex sockets, finer and denser turret knurling, deeper picatinny slots, a magazine with visible top cartridge/follower and a release latch

Photographic presentation: put the rifle on a surface (table, mat, ground) with contact shadows and bounce light, use a key/fill/rim photo setup with a softbox reflection on the metal, shallow depth of field and slight lens vignetting/grain for close-ups; the bipod must rest on a ground when deployed
Colour: chassis reads as light primer grey-green; push towards a real OD/FDE/black cerakote value and saturation with slight hue variation
